SI-4.answer: Lifespan Normative Modeling of Brain Microstructure

NM2-1.detail: Hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) was used to model the statistical distribution of derived WM metrics (FA, MD, AD, RD) as a function of age and sex, while accounting for site/scanner effects.
NM2-1.supporting_text: used hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) to model the statistical distribution of derived WM metrics as a function of age and sex.

NM2-2.detail: Normative models were built for fractional anisotropy (FA), and mean, radial, and axial diffusivity (MD/RD/AD) for 21 deep WM regions and the Global-WM.
NM2-2.supporting_text: We built normative models for the most widely used dMRI brain metrics - fractional anisotropy (FA), and mean, radial, and axial diffusivity (MD/RD/AD)

NM2-3.detail: Age (modeled with cubic b-splines), sex, and dMRI scanning protocol (as batch effect) were used as explanatory variables.
NM2-3.supporting_text: We added age and sex as the covariates for the present study and we modeled the non-linear effect of age with a cubic b-spline basis set expansion... Consequently, we used the dMRI protocol as the batch effect when training the normative model with HBR.
